ticket.title: The latest-anchor selector documents a `confirmedAt` tiebreak it does not implement — and since KS-1057 that selector decides the verdict
ticket.description:
# KS-1072 — Wednesday's task for Ornith (written from the ticket AND the code at develop M55 `48e65c435`, 2026-09-15 09:5x)

## What is wrong (one paragraph)
In `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts`, inside `makeFetchDocFromAnchorStore`, the "latest anchor"
selector's comment (line 287) promises: *"Latest = highest blockNumber, fall back to most-recent confirmedAt."*
The comparator on lines 288–289 implements only the first half — two anchors with the same `blockNumber` are
ordered arbitrarily, and since KS-1057 this selection decides the verdict. Implement the documented tiebreak.

## The exact change — ONE site, lines 288–289 only
Today (two physical lines):
```
              const latest = anchors.slice().sort((a: any, b: any) =>
                (b.blockNumber || 0) - (a.blockNumber || 0))[0];
```
Replace those two lines with a comparator that (1) orders by `blockNumber` descending as now, and (2) when the
block numbers are equal, orders by `confirmedAt` descending (most recent first), treating a missing/invalid
`confirmedAt` as the oldest:
```
              const latest = anchors.slice().sort((a: any, b: any) => {
                const byBlock = (b.blockNumber || 0) - (a.blockNumber || 0);
                if (byBlock !== 0) return byBlock;
                return (Date.parse(b.confirmedAt) || 0) - (Date.parse(a.confirmedAt) || 0);
              })[0];
```
Leave line 287's comment as it is (it is now true). Change NOTHING else in the file — no other line, no import.
The `anchors` array elements carry `blockNumber` (number) and `confirmedAt` (ISO string) — see line 343
(`latest.confirmedAt`) for the existing read of that field.

## The test — one new vitest file, in-process, no server
File: `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1072-latest-anchor-confirmedat-tiebreak.test.ts`
Copy the mocking shape from `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1071-verify-confidence-one-mapping.test.ts`
(it imports `../routes/verification` and drives it in-process over a stub anchor store: reuse how it stubs the
anchor-store HTTP reply so `data.data.anchors` is under the test's control). Cells:
- 🔴 `it('🔴 KS-1072 — equal blockNumber: the most recent confirmedAt wins')`: two anchors, both
  `blockNumber: 100`, A `confirmedAt: '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z'` with `id: 'anchor_old'`, B
  `confirmedAt: '2026-06-01T00:00:00Z'` with `id: 'anchor_new'`, listed OLD FIRST in the array; assert the
  selected/latest anchor is `anchor_new` (on the untouched code the stable sort keeps the first = old — the red).
- 🔴 `it('🔴 KS-1072 — a missing confirmedAt loses the tiebreak')`: same blockNumber, one anchor without
  `confirmedAt` listed first, one with a date second; assert the dated one wins.
- CONTROL `it('KS-1072 control — a higher blockNumber still wins regardless of confirmedAt')`: blockNumber 101
  with an old date vs 100 with a new date; assert the 101 anchor is selected before and after.
Assert through whatever the reference test asserts on (the verdict/anchor fields the route returns), not by
reaching into module internals.

## Where (parsed into the checklist — every **must change** line must appear as a `-` line in your diff)
* `:288` — **must change**: `              const latest = anchors.slice().sort((a: any, b: any) =>`
* `:289` — **must change**: `                (b.blockNumber || 0) - (a.blockNumber || 0))[0];`

## Output
Exactly ONE ```diff block; paths repo-relative (`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/...`); correct hunk
counts; blank context lines keep their leading space; the product hunk touches lines 288–289 only.
